questions.q: Choose the correct form: “If it had not been for your help last year, I ____ in that examination.”
questions.why: Third conditional for an unreal past situation. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In “The poor need our help,” the word “poor” functions as a:
questions.why: After 'the', it names a class of people, so it works as a noun. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: “Need I ____ the form again?”
questions.why: The modal 'need' in a question takes the bare infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In the sentence “He behaved as if he owned the place,” the clause “as if he owned the place” is a:
questions.why: 'As if' introduces an adverb clause of manner. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “The manager is liable ____ any loss to the company.”
questions.why: 'Liable for' a loss or damage. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “Since the clinic ____ in 2012, it has treated thousands of patients.”
questions.why: After 'since' the clause naming the starting point takes the simple past. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the part of speech of “only” in: “He is the only candidate who passed.”
questions.why: It modifies the noun 'candidate'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct version: “Many a patient have recovered after this treatment.”
opts: Many a patients has recovered after this treatment.
Many a patient has recovered after this treatment.
Many a patients have recovered after this treatment.
Many patient has recovered after this treatment.
questions.why: 'Many a' takes a singular noun and a singular verb. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “The doctor tried to ____ the anxious parents that the child was safe.”
questions.why: 'Assure' is used with a person; 'ensure' means to make certain. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Change into a complex sentence: “Having finished the work, he went home.”
opts: Before he had finished the work, he went home.
Although he finished the work, he went home.
Since he finished the work, he went home.
After he had finished the work, he went home.
questions.why: The participle phrase becomes a time clause with past perfect. GPSC-style practice item.
